newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls sharply against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls sharply against the dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Monday following the rise of the U.S. currency against the mark on overseas markets, dealers said.
"The shekel declined against the dollar as the U.S. currency rose sharply against the mark abroad following the French election," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.

"The rise of dollar pushed the basket of foreign currencies downwards and the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market on a relatively big scale buying more than $100 million to support the basket," he said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its trading band for four months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4060 shekels, against 3.3940 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6980 against 3.6962 Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9259 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9202 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9794 shekels compared with 1.9964 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4080 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
